review.alternative: Macroscopic objectivity could be an irreducible classical feature independent of quantum substrates.
review.would_change_mind: Observation of macroscopic objective states that violate quantum decoherence and einselection bounds.

claims.statement: The problem of objectivity explains the objective character of the macroscopic world via quantum-to-classical transitions.

support.explanation: Identifies the core inquiry into how macroscopic objectivity arises from quantum principles.
support.passage: The problem of objectivity, i.e. how to explain on quantum grounds the objective character of the macroscopic world, is one of the aspects of the celebrated quantum-to-classical transition.

review.alternative: All environmental redundancy is universally and equally accessible to any arbitrary observer without filtering.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that observer aperture functions do not restrict information recovery from the environment.

claims.statement: The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer.

support.explanation: Explicitly contrasts total environmental encoding with what an observer can access.
support.passage: The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer, models accessibility through a noisy-threshold aperture function
